beats.trigger: ## Getting Going
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: With the right guardrails, you create output that's genuinely yours, not generic.
beats.got: The promise is output that sounds like me, not like everyone else.

beats.trigger: Set up your agent runtime. Build a snake game as HTML.
beats.got: There was homework involving a snake game and my calendar. I can't see what that has to do with people work.

beats.trigger: **Package** the guardrails as reusable rules
beats.got: I will end up with some reusable rules, though I don't yet know what kind.

beats.trigger: where did LLM output on your own work come out generic, and what made it feel like yours?
beats.got: The question is about my own work. That I can answer, so I'm in.

beats.trigger: The same question. Two answers. What makes the difference?
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The first exchange became context.
beats.got: An earlier question quietly changes the answer to a later one, even when the two questions are unrelated.

beats.trigger: Change the front, change the back.
beats.got: The model rereads everything each time, so what I say early shapes everything after.

beats.trigger: You told the LLM who you are.
beats.got: Telling it my role changes what it suggests. This is how an HR partner could get answers fitted to her situation.

beats.trigger: Tools, goals, checks, boundaries, and loops come later and depend on it.
beats.got: There are more parts coming that nobody has explained yet. That's jargon before explanation.

beats.trigger: You write it once, and it shapes every answer.
beats.got: I can write context down once in a file. That is how a habit could spread from one person to a team.

beats.trigger: Change the context, watch the agent's output shift, then package what you learned for the next session.
beats.got: I'll change the input, watch what comes out, and then save what I learned.

beats.trigger: Take the whole page, headers and sidebar included.
beats.got: I paste my own LinkedIn page and get a bland site back. It's fine for me, but I'm a bit wary of what happens to the text.

beats.trigger: A colleague who lands on it should think *"this is the person I want to work with more, on the things they're great at,"*
beats.got: The site should make colleagues want to work with me, not sell to them.

beats.trigger: **name the framework, tune it, ask the agent to run it.**
beats.got: I can name a framework I already know and tell the agent to adjust it, without explaining the whole thing.

beats.trigger: Answer each in your own words, briefly; don't polish.
beats.got: The agent interviews me one question at a time and rebuilds the page from my short answers.

beats.trigger: Your strengths shape how the whole site sounds.
beats.got: I list my strengths and the site's tone changes.

beats.trigger: Most people can list what drives them mad at work in thirty seconds, but stall for five minutes on what they're great at.
beats.got: It's easier to say what I'm against than what I'm for, and the inverted list gives me a clearer self-description.

beats.trigger: Vague input drifts back to the statistical-default you.
beats.got: If I give specific irritations, the output sounds like me. If I stay vague, it sounds average.

beats.trigger: LLMs go easy on their own output.
beats.got: The agent is too kind about its own work, so I need a harsher second look.

beats.trigger: *"Make it look like Stripe's design language"*
beats.got: I can borrow a famous site's look just by naming it. Playing with that was fun.

beats.trigger: a fresh agent can repeat it on someone else's bio without you re-explaining
beats.got: What I did gets saved as a rules file that another agent can reuse on someone else's bio. That's the part I could hand to my HR partners.

beats.trigger: The more specific the context, the more the output is yours.
beats.got: Every phase added more specific context about me, and the output got more specific.

beats.trigger: anywhere the question is "is this genuinely ours or just fine?"
beats.got: The same move applies to company work like proposals and reviews, not only a personal site. Role descriptions would be one of those.

beats.trigger: ## Iterate and Learn
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: which rule should survive into the next session.
beats.got: What I want to keep from today is a short list of rules for the next session.

beats.trigger: Grading its own work is another chance to be helpful
beats.got: The agent flatters its own work because it was trained to be agreeable.

beats.trigger: Where the account matches what you remember, you have two reads agreeing.
beats.got: I treat the agent's report as a claim to check against what I saw. I trust it more where it matches my memory.

beats.trigger: Only you could catch a wrong line about you
beats.got: I am the one who knows what is true about me, so my judgment is the check.

beats.trigger: Nobody knows where agents are going, not Anthropic, not your board.
beats.got: Doing it yourself beats reading reports. The line about my board is true, but it's the only nod to leadership and doesn't give me anything to bring them.

beats.trigger: The first pass is rarely right.
beats.got: The agent re-reads my rules file against the session and rewrites it.

beats.trigger: **compound interest on a rule file.**
beats.got: I should push back on the agent's retro, and each round makes the rules file better.

beats.trigger: Your gut on what is uniquely you carries more weight than the agent's.
beats.got: A separate fresh reader gives a second opinion, and my own gut still outranks both.

beats.trigger: Output got specific because the context did.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Bring a live challenge and working access to Confluence and OneDrive.
beats.got: I need a real problem and access to our documents for next time.

beats.trigger: Karpathy's LLM Wiki post; Lindenberg's memory-architecture piece, optional.
beats.got: There are two optional reads, and I'll probably skip them.

beats.trigger: Arrive with enough real material that the memory starts from your world, not generic output.
beats.got: Next time I need real material from my own work.

beats.trigger: If stuck, scan your next two weeks of calendar; the biggest unresolved item is usually your challenge.
beats.got: I choose my challenge from my calendar. For me it will be a people question, for example how roles change.

beats.trigger: If a connector needs admin approval, tell the training coordinator and keep going.
beats.got: The agent should read our wiki and shared drive. Nobody says that HR files would need the works council and the DPO first, and I haven't asked either.

beats.trigger: ask it for a plan and approve or revise it first.
beats.got: I can make the agent show a plan and approve it before it writes files. That's a control I could explain to others.

beats.trigger: If a line is blank, name a fallback; do not fill it with a plausible answer.
beats.got: I write down my challenge, a source and a planning control in one file. If I don't have one, I name a fallback and don't bluff.

beats.trigger: a useful system is a living pile of text the agent can read, maintain, and improve.
beats.got: Memory is just text files the agent reads and updates.

beats.trigger: The output now travels with a file the agent re-reads next time.
beats.got: Next time builds on the file I made today.

take_homes: What I tell the AI first steers every answer after it. Specific things about me, like what annoys me at work, make the output sound like mine.
Writing the context into a file means it applies every time, and that file could be shared. I could use that for my HR partners.
The agent grades its own work too kindly, so I check it against what I know and ask a fresh reader for a second opinion.

monday.move: Ask one HR business partner what a role-description rules file for their area would contain, and draft a first version together.
monday.stop_condition: If it needs real employee data. Then I stop and ask the works council and the DPO first.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I still haven't asked them.

misconception.why: The module was about personal output and never touched roles, hiring or headcount, so my view that roles go first is the same as when I came in.

one_line: Good hands-on lesson in how to get the AI to sound like you, but it never says what any of this means for the people in my organisation.
